chunks: Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: regarding

A man who commits an offense outside the Haram, then seeks refuge in the Haram—he said: “The hadd is not carried out upon him, and he is not to be fed, nor given drink, nor spoken to, nor traded with. For when that is done to him, he will soon come out, and then the hadd will be carried out upon him. But if he commits an offense in the Haram, the hadd is carried out upon him in the Haram, for he did not regard the Haram as having sanctity.”

key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: the sacred sanctuary whose inviolability carries legal consequences
key_terms.جِنَايَةً: an offense or crime entailing liability

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on someone who commits a crime outside the Haram and then seeks refuge inside it?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal ruling concerning one who commits a crime outside the Haram and then takes refuge within it. The sanctity of the Haram prevents immediate enforcement there for an outside offense, but social and commercial pressure is applied until the person leaves; however, if the offense is committed within the Haram itself, the hadd is enforced there because the offender violated its sanctity.
